key_evidence: Why it matters: Portugal's published score of 60.6 sits just 0.6 points above the line between Established and Functional. New evidence about how police handled housing protests takes it below that line.
Before dawn on 20 October 2026, police cleared housing-protest camps in Lisbon and Porto in one national operation. They detained 55 people (Reuters).

The national police (PSP) called the clearance 'calm, proportionate'. Protesters said they were hit on the head. Amnesty International asked on 15 October 2026 for an independent inquiry into an earlier Porto clearance.
Parliament backed a bill on 30 September 2026 that would speed up evictions and end rent controls on new leases.
Portugal measures 59.4 of 100 (Functional). This is a band crossing, so a proposal is filed. Its sources are news reports and Amnesty, none at tier 4 or above, so it is filed as flag-for-review.

notes: Filed on the band-crossing clause at a sub-5-point delta (-1.2), per the 2026-08-16 Djibouti/Mauritania precedent. Moves: E4 4->3 (police framed injuries as 'resistance'; Amnesty asked for an independent inquiry), I1 4->3 (national camp clearance, 55 detained, minister declared camps over), EQ2 4->3 (30 Sep 2026 first-reading approval of a bill speeding evictions and ending rent caps on new leases). The prior E4 and I1 values of 4 had no URL-backed evidence; EQ2's 4 rested on the EIB housing loan (tier 4, positive), which is kept as evidence. Two of the three moves are needed to cross 60.0 (one move alone gives 60.6). RC-3: the 32 seed-carried subdimensions without URLs are unchanged; at 2 the composite is 31.3, at 3 it is 51.2, both Functional or lower, so the crossing does not depend on the convention. Lisbon/Porto municipal conduct is scored under those cities; PSP is national and scored here. ACT 3.6 against the published 3.4 is carried unchanged from the 2026-09-14 measurement (EIB housing loan, AC2/AC4 at 4, tier-4 source) and is not a new upward move.
